exposure: non-Hispanic Native Hawaiian/Other Pacific Islander ethnicity
outcome: not admitted to neonatal intensive care units (NICU)
cohort: The cohort consisted of 38,693 very preterm (<32 weeks gestation) and very low birth weight (<1500 grams) infants recorded in the National Vital Statistics System in 2021.
finding: Among very preterm, very low birth weight infants, 10% were not admitted to the NICU, with non-Hispanic Native Hawaiian/Other Pacific Islander ethnicity, gestational age 22-24 weeks, vaginal delivery, and a 5-minute Apgar score of 0-3 being associated with a higher prevalence of non-admission.
mod_finding: Vaginal delivery was associated with a higher prevalence of very preterm, very low birth weight infants not being admitted to the NICU.
